title: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean theorem and its converse

sections.skill: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean theorem and its converse

questions.skill: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean theorem and its converse
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: The figure shows a square with sides a + b, made of four right triangles and a tilted square with side c. Explain how the figure proves that a² + b² = c².
questions.prompt_markup:
The figure shows a square with sides a + b, made of four right triangles and a tilted square with side c.
Explain how the figure proves that a² + b² = c².
questions.required_method: A complete argument: the large square's area is (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²; it is also 4 triangles (4 · {1/2}ab = 2ab) plus the inner square c²; so a² + 2ab + b² = 2ab + c², and subtracting 2ab gives a² + b² = c². Any equivalent wording is accepted.

questions.skill: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean theorem and its converse
questions.prompt: A triangle has sides a, b, and c with a² + b² = c². Explain why it must be a right triangle.
questions.prompt_markup: A triangle has sides a, b, and c with a² + b² = c². Explain why it must be a right triangle.
questions.correct_answer: A right triangle with legs a and b has a hypotenuse of √(a² + b²) = c. So the two triangles have the same three sides and are congruent (SSS), and the given triangle has a right angle too.

questions.skill: Prove the Pythagorean theorem with similar triangles
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC with the right angle at C, altitude CD is drawn to hypotenuse AB. Why is AC² = AD · AB?
questions.prompt_markup:
In right triangle ABC with the right angle at C, altitude CD is drawn to hypotenuse AB.
Why is AC² = AD · AB?
questions.correct_answer: Triangle ACD is similar to triangle ABC (AA), so AC/AB = AD/AC, which gives AC² = AD · AB.

questions.skill: Prove the Pythagorean theorem with similar triangles
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: In the same triangle, BC² = BD · AB. Add this to AC² = AD · AB. What do you get?
questions.prompt_markup: In the same triangle, BC² = BD · AB. Add this to AC² = AD · AB. What do you get?
questions.correct_answer: AC² + BC² = AD · AB + BD · AB = AB(AD + BD) = AB · AB = AB².
